It uses dbusUtility::readDbusProperty(), this is extra fitting before dubs::utility.

Doxygen:
 * It extracts chassis ID from FRU inventory path and constructs appropriate
 * chassis/system inventory path based on Fcs/Mts type location code.

I can think of re-naming

I agree with @souvikroyofficial10@gmail.com 
Why do we need another DBus API for just reading the value from DBus? Extraction of chassis ID is a one line operation, can be done at the place of calling itself.

Extraction of chassis ID is a one line operation, >
Extraction of chassisID -> create a chassis inventory path -> call objectMapper-> extract the service from it and use it for bus call to read the keyword value.


And this will increase the length of API.

this can be done. but we had this kind of utility functions already in place, which is told to remove in story description. so I didn't handle it in 2 separate helper functions.

either extract as immediate I need it.
Or pass it from chain of functions.
I chose 1st one.
@sunnsr25@in.ibm.com Your opinion please.

@alpu8007@gmail.com As you are already passing that parameter to another functions, passing it again to "processExtraInterfaces" will keep things consistent and it will save the call to "contains" and "extraction of inventory path from the JSON map" that you are doing inside the API "processExtraInterfaces".

As it requires no extra changes to pass "inventoryPath" as parameter. I will opt for the option where I will pass as parameter.

ok, sure.
will change it to pass as parameter,
Better heading please

Why all these were done?
Done

Suggestion: We can use `std::expected<std::string,uint16_t>` as the return type. In success path, the expanded location code will be returned and on failure error code will be returned. This avoids returning unexpanded location code in error path and makes the return value more usable to the caller.

Based on use cases here, we don't treat  failure error code  as a blocker.
caller uses returned data(expanded/unexpanded) directly.  if error code != 0 then log a message.
If we go with std::expected<std::string,uint16_t>, we need special handling here-
In good case- use returned data, in error case- use what input was given.
I think current design is simpler.

I see the `i_inventoryPath` parameter is only being used to log in failure case. Do we really need the inventory path in this log? Or is there any other use case of passing inventory path to this API?
yes, we need this i_inventoryPath . check https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/openpower-vpd-parser/+/91930/9/vpd-manager/include/utility/vpd_specific_utility.hpp
